[ota-hal] OTA-1790 — the exchange reads as a sentence

The reference pack's central instruction: *"The current transcript contains the
right facts but makes the player reconstruct the event from fragments. Replace
the math/problem-reading presentation with plain-language event reporting."*
Its target, verbatim: `YOU HIT Conspiracy Architect 1 for 25 HP`. Its
prohibition, verbatim: *"Do not show the old equation-like fragments, duplicated
actor/outcome labels, arrows, or disconnected damage values when the same
information can be read as one sentence."*

WHAT SHIPPED WAS ALL FOUR OF THOSE, AND IT COST TWO ROWS PER SWING. One player
attack writes TWO log lines — the to-hit verdict and then the damage — and
VIS-2's strip drew each as its own instrument row:

    YOU > Raider                     HIT
    YOU > Raider                     HIT   25
      Rusted Blade          Raider 12/40

Duplicated actor labels, a duplicated stamp, an arrow, and a damage value
marooned in a column eight positions away from the words that explain it.

WHAT THE PASS ACTUALLY DOES

  A. THE EVENT LINE. `engine/combatSentence.eventLine` turns one authoritative
     `CombatEvent` into the pack's sentence as ORDERED PARTS — subject, verb,
     object, damage tail, note, standing readout — so a renderer can colour a
     part without ever being the thing that decides word order. Two rulings
     inside it are worth naming:
       * A DEFENSIVE OUTCOME IS REPORTED FROM THE DEFENDER'S SIDE. `side` says
         who swung; on a dodge nobody cares who swung. `Raider DODGED YOU`,
         `YOU EVADED Raider` — the pack's own example is written that way.
       * `crit` AND `fumble` BECOME A NOTE, NOT A VERB. "YOU CRIT Raider" is
         jargon and "YOU FUMBLED Raider" is not English. Both keep the emphasis
         VIS-2 reserved for them, as `— CRITICAL` / `— FUMBLE`.
     The pack's zero-damage case is implemented verbatim:
     `Conspiracy Architect 1 HIT YOU for 0 HP — ARMOUR ABSORBED`.

  B. THE FOLD. `foldExchanges` pairs each to-hit verdict with the damage line
     reporting the same exchange and drops the verdict's row, keeping its roll.
     Two passes, because order is not negotiable — a one-pass version has to HOLD
     a verdict it might later emit, and an unconsumed verdict would surface at
     the wrong place in the feed. The match is narrow (same side, same
     counterpart, no intervening verdict for that combatant), because a
     five-raider round interleaves and a loose match would staple one raider's
     roll onto another raider's blow. An EXCEPTIONAL verdict wins over the
     damage line's plain outcome — the resolver writes `crit` on the swing and
     `hit` on the damage, so a naive merge would silently demote every critical
     hit in the game.

  C. THE WEAPON MARK. `weaponFamilyArt` (OTA-1789) finally has a consumer. The
     family is resolved AT THE SWING from the catalog row `getEquippedWeapon`
     returns — never from `weaponName`, which is a display string and may carry a
     coating prefix; the pack forbids prose string matching by name. Bare hands
     are a family rather than a missing weapon (`swungFamily(row, bareHanded)`).
     The mark is 20dp because the event line is 14/20 and one line box is exactly
     what a subordinate mark may cost — the pack allowed a smaller governed
     density than 28 explicitly, and this is a derivation rather than a taste
     call. The column is RESERVED whether or not there is a picture.

  D. LAYER B. The consequence in words, naming the actual weapon, riding on the
     EVENT rather than replacing `entry.text`. The resolver still writes its full
     sentence — every number in it — so the disk log, the LOG export and the
     playtest reports read exactly as they did. One authority, two audiences.
     `enemyStrikeProse` takes `armour` as an argument rather than guessing:
     *"Your armour turns the blow aside"* is a claim about mechanics and must be
     true when it is printed.

  E. THE COATING. Named only at the proc site, where a roll actually landed, and
     drawn with the DAMAGE/COATING glyph family — never the weapon one. The pack:
     *"Weapon glyph = what delivered the attack. Damage/coating glyph = what kind
     of damage/effect occurred. Do not collapse those concepts into one icon."*

THE EXTRACTION, AND WHY IT WAS THE PRICE OF ADMISSION

`check:storeceiling` sat at 36,998 of 36,998 with NO headroom, and this pass
needed lines the store did not have. The owner's ruling was *"EXTRACT, DO NOT
JUST RAISE IT"*. Five pure functions of (weapon, name, damage) — `weaponPhrase`,
`attackOpener`, `attackHit`, `attackMiss`, `attackKill` — were living at the
bottom of a 37,000-line store; `engine/combatProse.ts` was already named for
exactly them and already declared the rule they obey. They moved verbatim: same
words, same pools, same order, so every line the game has ever printed still
prints. The store went 36,998 -> 36,963 and the CEILING came down onto the
measurement. This is the first time that number has fallen as a CONDITION OF
WORK rather than as tidying, which is the pressure the valve exists to create.

WHAT CHANGED THAT SOMEBODY MIGHT MISS

  * `row-reverse` IS GONE. VIS-2 flipped the whole incoming row to move the
    spine to the far side. A reserved glyph column cannot survive that — the mark
    lands on a different x on every incoming blow and the column stops being one.
    BOTH edges are reserved now and exactly one is lit: 4px buys back the same
    non-chromatic "which way did this go", and the mark's x is identical in both
    directions rather than merely close. VIS-2's third structural cue (the
    indent) is retired with it; the sentence's own word order replaces it and is
    the strongest of the four, being English rather than a convention to learn.
  * THE NAME IS NO LONGER CLAMPED TO ONE LINE. Deliberately reversed, on the
    pack's instruction: *"Allow long enemy names to wrap/truncate according to a
    governed rule without scrambling HIT/target/damage order."* The governed rule
    is WRAP. This is also what closes OTA-1772's defect class structurally — you
    cannot weld a stamp to an ellipsis when there is neither.
  * A LANDED BLOW IS NOW ONE ROW, NOT TWO. VIS-2's density measurement improves;
    ota1745's assertion was re-aimed upward rather than relaxed.
  * THE SCREEN READER GETS THE SAME SENTENCE THE EYE DOES. It used to get
    "YOU attacks Raider: HIT, 25 damage" — a third phrasing invented in the
    component.

FINDING, REPORTED NOT FIXED — THE ENEMY HAS NO WEAPON FAMILY

`Enemy` carries `attack` and `damage` as dice strings and nothing that names an
object. The only weapon-shaped fact in reach is `enemyDamageType`, and deriving a
sword from "slashing" would make the mark a DAMAGE-TYPE icon, which the pack says
in so many words the weapon glyph is not. So incoming exchanges reserve the
column and leave it empty, per the pack's own fail-safe rule, and a test pins the
gap so a later pass has to argue with it rather than quietly fill it in.

THREE SHIPPED SUITES WERE RE-AIMED AT THEIR CLAIMS, NOT DELETED

ota1772 (the stamp/name collision), ota1745 (density and the one-second read).
Every re-aim is annotated in place with what changed and why, including the one
claim this pass deliberately REVERSED (the one-line name clamp). Where a claim
became structurally impossible, the test now asserts the impossibility — which is
a stronger guard than the layout assertion it replaces.

Grade the code, not the prose — 28th sighting. This file's own header quotes the
fragments it deleted (`YOU > Raider`, the arrow, the stamp), so a scanner reading
raw source would report the defect as still present. The suite carries a
`codeOf()` stripper plus an assertion that the RAW file still names them.

23/23 gates green. Full surface green.
